channel.title: Learn to Upholster
channel.description: The Working Upholsterer’s Bible by Shaun Greenwood — traditional and modern upholstery, free to read.

item.title: What you should never use on upholstery
item.description: Most upholstery damage is caused by cleaning, not by use. The products that quietly wreck fabric and leather, why the hidden-patch test only half works, and what the W, S and X codes on your label mean.

item.title: Care & Cleaning
item.description: Blog posts on care & cleaning from a working upholsterer’s bench.

item.title: Do you need formal training to become an upholsterer?
item.description: Legally, no — upholstery is unregulated and anyone can trade tomorrow. What training actually buys you, what it does not, and the obligations that apply whether you trained or not.

item.title: Learning the Trade
item.description: Blog posts on learning the trade from a working upholsterer’s bench.

item.title: Why is my sofa fabric bobbling?
item.description: Pilling is loose fibre working to the surface, and it is usually not a fault. Why blends pill worst, why it normally stops on its own, and the separate test standard nobody tells you to ask about.

item.title: Why do two upholsterers quote such different prices?
item.description: Usually because they are not quoting for the same work. The recover-versus-reupholster distinction, what gets replaced underneath, and the five questions that make quotes actually comparable.

item.title: How to look after a leather sofa
item.description: Which finish you have decides everything, and there is a two-minute test that tells you. The routine that keeps leather alive for decades, and the everyday products that quietly destroy it.

item.title: What's the best upholstery fabric if you have a dog?
item.description: The construction matters more than the fibre. Why loops are the thing to avoid, which fabrics genuinely survive claws and hair, and the colour trick nobody mentions.

item.title: Is it cheaper to reupholster or buy new?
item.description: Usually not, if you compare it to the cheapest new sofa in the sale — but that is the wrong comparison. What actually decides it is the frame, and how to check yours in two minutes.

item.title: Buying & Costs
item.description: Blog posts on buying & costs from a working upholsterer’s bench.

item.title: Why has my sofa gone saggy in the middle?
item.description: Something under the cushions has failed, and it is usually not the cushions. How to tell whether it is the foam, the webbing, the springs or the frame — and which of those is worth fixing.

item.title: Problems & Repairs
item.description: Blog posts on problems & repairs from a working upholsterer’s bench.

item.title: Why does velvet go patchy?
item.description: Velvet does not go patchy — it shades. Why pile fabric changes colour as it is pressed, which velvets recover and which mark permanently, and what pile direction does to your fabric quantity.

item.title: Fabrics
item.description: Blog posts on fabrics from a working upholsterer’s bench.

item.title: Blog
item.description: Notes from the workshop bench: materials, problems, and the questions customers actually ask.

item.title: Why does leather peel?
item.description: Real leather does not peel. What peels is bonded leather or a polyurethane coating — how to tell which you have, why it fails, and what can actually be repaired.

item.title: Leather & Vinyl
item.description: Blog posts on leather & vinyl from a working upholsterer’s bench.

item.title: United States upholstery fire regulations
item.description: Federal standard since 2021, and it names reupholstery — but not when the piece keeps the same owner.

item.title: Upholstery fire regulations by country
item.description: Upholstery fire regulations by country: United Kingdom, United States, Canada, Australia & New Zealand. Domestic and commercial requirements, sourced and date

item.title: Australia & New Zealand upholstery fire regulations
item.description: The AS/NZS upholstery flammability standards are voluntary. There is no mandatory domestic requirement in either country.

item.title: Canada upholstery fire regulations
item.description: No flammability standard for upholstered furniture. All three provincial schemes were repealed between 2019 and 2021.

item.title: Ireland upholstery fire regulations
item.description: Its own 1995 Order and Irish Standard, close to the British regime but a separate legal instrument.

item.title: Jensen S-V8 — Fitting a New Car Carpet Set in Navy — Upholstery Project
item.description: Replacing a car carpet set is a patterning job before it is a fitting job: strip the interior, lift the worn original out whole, and cut the new one to its shape.
